analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 8 Oct 2026
key_insights: Prime book data shows US Tech stocks had their largest % buying in a month since Feb '25 in September, and Tech was the only sector net bought on the prime book that month.
Net exposure on the GS prime book to Mag7, as a % of total US exposure, is near 22%, the highest on record since the start of 2022. Overall market net positioning is still low.
Semis and Semi Equipment are now about 12% of total US exposure on the prime book, versus a June peak of 14% and about 6% at the start of the year.

September FOMC minutes: all participants supported a 25bp hike to 3.75-4%, saying progress on lowering inflation had not been sufficient. Almost all saw inflation risks tilted to the upside, and labour market risks were seen as diminished and broadly balanced.

Many FOMC participants described the hike as prudent on risk-management grounds, while a number saw it as necessary under their modal outlook. Most judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year end, with each meeting approached with an open mind.

GS expects the second Fed hike in December, after the August core PCE data and speeches by Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams. GS also sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary.
Tuesday's session was muted and lower with defensive posturing (NDX > SPX > RTY) as global yields kept backing up. The GS US Cyclicals vs. Defensives pair traded -159bps.

Russell underperformed NDX for the 4th straight day and 17 times in the last 20 sessions, as small caps bear the brunt of higher rates. A 39bn 10-year auction priced 1.6bps through at 5.3% (vs 5.316% going in) and gave some afternoon relief.
GS floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, driven mostly by macro products and to a smaller extent tech.

GS Online Travel Q3 preview: industry data and channel checks point to broadly stable to strong end demand, most pronounced in the US in the September quarter. Investor focus is on forward commentary and unit pricing, how management frames agentic AI opportunities and challenges, and growth investment versus 2027 operating margin.

GS energy services update covers BKR, SLB, FTI and HAL ahead of Q3 earnings. GS shows a relative preference for BKR, citing its more defensive, industrial-driven model, upside to 2027 consensus estimates, IET backlog conversion and a production-oriented OFSE business.

GS highlights FTI for backlog resilience and is looking for more colour on the 2027 order outlook. Across OFS coverage the focus is Middle East oilfield activity disruptions, customer conversations and services pricing.

LEVI F3Q reported revenue growth of +4.3% missed GS (+4.5%) and consensus (+4.7%), as wholesale and international strength was offset by softer US and Europe DTC. Management said global DTC is running +MSD% quarter to date, with US DTC back to growth and Europe back to MSD% growth.

LEVI raised FY26 EPS and EBIT margin guidance, but the new outlook includes a net benefit from tariff refunds and higher SG&A from reinvestment and elevated distribution costs. Management expects FY26 to be the peak year for distribution transition costs, which opens room for gross margin expansion in FY27.

Today's calendar: Fed Governor Waller speaks at 09:30 UK time. Initial jobless claims for the week ended October 3 are due (GS 200k, consensus 200k, last 197k), then August final wholesale inventories. PEP reports pre-market.

Preview describes a broadly stable to strong end demand environment, strongest in the US in the September quarter. Price targets updated, no sector stance change stated.

earnings_insights: LEVI F3Q reported revenue growth +4.3% (reported 10/7 print), below GS estimate +4.5% and consensus estimate +4.7%.
LEVI raised FY26 EPS and EBIT margin guidance. The updated outlook includes a net benefit from tariff refunds and higher SG&A, reflecting reinvestment and elevated distribution costs.

LEVI management reiterated its +MSD% revenue growth and margin expansion algorithm and expects FY26 to be the peak for distribution transition-related costs, supporting gross margin expansion into FY27.
LEVI global DTC is running +MSD% quarter to date in F4Q, with US DTC back to positive growth and Europe back to MSD% growth.

Online Travel Q3 earnings preview: GS refreshes operating estimates and 12-month price targets. Key debates are forward commentary on elevated unit pricing, agentic AI framing, and growth investment versus 2027 margins.
Energy services estimates updated for BKR, SLB, FTI and HAL ahead of Q3. GS sees upside to 2027 consensus estimates for BKR.
PEP reports pre-market today. No other earnings are scheduled post-market.
